title: Pinegrove Insurance — private deployment consolidation & TF migration scenarios (draft)
content:
Context:

This is a working draft for Pinegrove Insurance’s private deployment consolidation and migration from their existing hybrid inference stack into Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem options). Purpose is to capture sizing proposals, Terraform module adaptation notes, phased cutover scenarios, and outstanding architecture questions/assumptions. Not client-ready — internal review + validation required.

High-level goals (customer asks):
- Move inference traffic for policy-doc parsing and claims triage from 3rd-party hosted endpoints to a customer-managed VPC with dedicated Redwood Private runtime in two data centers (primary + DR).
- Guarantee P99 latency < 120ms for short-chat/response workloads and sustained throughput of 300 QPS across peak windows with ability to autoscale to 500 QPS.
- Integrate with customer KMS for key management and field-level data obfuscation.
- Maintain rolling upgrades with zero downtime and automated fallback to hosted model variants if local capacity is saturated.

Assumptions (please flag during review):
- Models: using a family of open-weights 16B and 70B variants (float16). Typical Lmax 1024 tokens, median output length 40 tokens.
- Quantization target: customer requires aggressive cost optimization; plan to support q4_0/q4f16 options. Evaluation will be required for quality drift.
- Network: Pinegrove will provide VPC peering/Transit Gateway and route tables; we will not manage their on-prem networking devices.
- Storage: model artifacts stored in S3-compatible object store (on-prem MinIO) with 3 replicas across racks.
- Certificate management: customer uses Vault for internal certs; we integrate for TLS termination on control plane endpoints.

Sizing proposal (initial):
Phase 1 baseline (steady-state 300 QPS):
- Serving nodes: 6 x H100-80GB (or equivalent) per primary site. Rationale: 6 nodes provide sustained concurrency for batching + parallel streams; each H100 estimated to serve ~50 QPS at median request sizes with q4 quantized models.
- KV cache nodes: 2 x A40 (GPU-less or small-GPU) for large shared embeddings/KV cache tiers to lower duplicate compute.
- Control/management: 3 x m5.large equivalents (control plane VMs) for autoscaler, router, and monitoring agents in the VPC control plane.
- Storage/cache: 4 x NVMe servers for local model cache and shard storage (pull-through from MinIO).
- DR site: reserve 3 x H100 for fast failover (hot-standby) and reduced autoscale.

Phase 2 (scale to 500 QPS & SLA):
- Add 4 H100 nodes at primary; enable cross-site active-active routing for latency-sensitive traffic.
- Increase KV tier to 4 nodes.
- Add dedicated logging/observability cluster for 30d retention.

Sizing notes and tolerances: numbers are conservative — we should run a few replay traces from Pinegrove to validate. If models are smaller (16B) and quantized aggressively, H100 requirement can drop to A100/80GB equivalents and fewer nodes.

Terraform module adaptation notes (high level):
- Existing Redwood TF modules assume cloud object store. Add abstractions for on-prem MinIO backend (S3-compatible) with endpoint, access_key, secret_key inputs.
- Network modules: create a "customer_peering" submodule that accepts Transit Gateway / Peer IDs OR on-prem static routes. Keep both options; customers often provide VPN instead of TGW.
- KMS integration: new module to wire in external KMS (HashiCorp Vault or vendor HSM). This must create placeholders for encryptionKeyId but not attempt to provision KMS resources.
- Instance profiles: parametrized GPU type var.gpu_instance_type so module can create H100/A100/A40 ASGs (or PKS on-prem equivalents).
- Cutover hooks: add lifecycle null_resource with remote-exec hooks for pre-cutover sanity checks (model checksum verify), and post-cutover smoke test (healthcheck query against a canary prompt).
- Terraform state: recommend remote state in customer-controlled backend (consul or S3 + locking) — document recommended retention/backups.

Upgrade & cutover plan (phased, zero-downtime intent):
1) Prep & validation (2–3 weeks)
   - Provision baseline infra in a staging VPC with terraform plans applied to a non-prod MinIO bucket.
   - Deploy Redwood Private runtime behind test LB, push models, run synthetic load tests using customer's trace.
   - Run function/format integration tests with policy data samples (PII redaction flows).

2) Canary in production VPC (1 week)
   - Route 1–3% of traffic to new site via weighted routing.
   - Monitor latency, error rates, and quality regression.
   - If quality drift > threshold (configurable) then revert routing and increase quantization fidelity.

3) Progressive rollout (1–2 weeks)
   - Increase routing in 10–20% increments during low-traffic windows.
   - Run controlled rollback drill after each increment.

4) Full cutover + hardening
   - Switch DNS/CNAME and decommission old endpoints after 72h stable metrics.

5) Post-cutover (30 days)
   - Stability and quality monitoring. Schedule a controlled model quantization experiment to search for cost/quality sweet spot.

Rollback scenarios and safe states:
- If model quality regression is detected at canary >5% of baseline eval set (client-provided), immediately shift traffic back to hosted variant and mark the deployment as "degraded" in the console.
- If infra resource exhaustion occurs (GPU OOM or kernel failures), autoscaler should reduce batch sizes and fall back to lower-concurrency endpoints — document precise autoscaler policy thresholds.

Open architecture questions / action items (team):
- Q1: Pinegrove insists on using customer HSM for private keys. Does Redwood need to store any key material long-term, or can all key wrapping be delegated? ACTION: Leah to confirm HSM vendor model and integration surface.
- Q2: What traffic shaping does Pinegrove require for internal vs external callers (e.g., real-time support chatbot vs async document ingestion)? ACTION: Sales/SE to get peak-per-route QPS breakdown.
- Q3: Are there compliance constraints that prohibit model artifact caching on local NVMe? If yes, need an encrypted ephemeral model loader path. ACTION: Devon to raise with Security.
- Q4: Are there existing Terraform conventions/registry at Pinegrove we should align with (module naming, tagging, run policies)? ACTION: Marco to request sample repo.

Quality evaluation plan (for quantization):
- Baseline: run 1k example prompts from production trace through float16 model to get baseline BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity scores and human spot-checks.
- Test q4_0 and q4f16 variants across same prompts; compute delta distributions and flag worst 10% regressions for manual review.
- If drift concentrated in hallucination/long-context answers, increase precision for decoder layers only (mixed-precision).

Operational runbook snippets (quick wins):
- Model checksum: "sha256sum <artifact>" on model pull; abort if mismatch.
- Healthcheck endpoint: /internal/health responds with {uptime, gpu_util, kv_hit_rate}. Alert if gpu_util>85% for 10m and kv_hit_rate<30%.
- Emergency scale: a terraform apply with var.auto_scale_override=true should add 2 H100 nodes across AZs within 12m.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regression after quantization. Mitigation: staggered rollouts, canary evals, automated rollback.
- Risk: Network egress constraints cause cold-starts for model fetch. Mitigation: pre-warm cache and allow stash replication window.
- Risk: Customer-run Terraform drift. Mitigation: recommend periodic reconciliation run (weekly) from Redwood ops account with read-only auditing.

Next steps (internal):
- Collect Pinegrove trace + representative eval set (SE request).
- Leah to confirm KMS/HSM vendor details and compliance constraints by 2025-10-09.
- Marco to provide Terraform repo layout and tagging policy by 2025-10-07.
- Schedule 90-minute architecture review with Pinegrove infra + security (proposed: 2025-10-13).

Notes to reviewer: This doc intentionally mixes high-level customer facing language with infra-level TODOs so we can hand off to Solutions Eng. Remove internal ACTIONs before sharing externally unless those owners are comfortable.

End of draft.
